name: RfPatrol Mk2 body-worn RF detector (DroneShield)
description: Body-worn, strictly non-emitting RF detector. 4 km in a low-RF (rural) background but only 1 km in a high-RF (urban) background. Directional and omnidirectional antennas give 360 deg cover. Alerts by sound, light and haptic.

detectRangeM.condition: up to 4000 m in a rural environment, no target class stated
detectRangeM.source: Army Recognition, Droneshield releases handheld RfPatrol Mk II drone detector (2020)

classifyRangeM.condition: protocol identification range — No separate classification range published. DroneShield states the device provides 'real-time drone signal detection, identification, and classification' from one receive event, so classify is set equal to the rural detect figure. INFERRED.

rangeAccuracyM.note: A single-site RF direction finder measures bearing, not range; not established by the public record.

azimuthAccuracyDeg.note: Class median of the sourced early-warning RF detectors (a body-worn signal-strength bearing, like the RfPatrol directional antenna): lib-wingman 30; median 30 deg.

elevationAccuracyDeg.note: Two-dimensional RF direction finding gives no elevation; not established by the public record.

receiverSensitivityDbm.note: Planning factor, 2.4 GHz band, channel-integrated: kTB for a 10 MHz OcuSync-class channel (-104 dBm) plus a 12 dB receiver noise figure (Narda SignalShark C-UAS application note) gives -92 dBm, recorded as -90 dBm. The body-worn unit's smaller antenna lowers its gain, not its receiver sensitivity. DroneShield publishes no sensitivity (droneshield.com/products-dismounted).

geolocationMinNodes.note: Omnidirectional body-worn detector: alarm by signal strength, no bearing and no multi-node geolocation documented (DroneShield dismounted products page); bearing-only at best, so no node count applies.
